logicalBugs.explanation: The Workflows list offers and confirms bulk Name updates, but submitting them always returns “Method not allowed” and leaves the selected workflows unchanged.

rootCause.explanation: The generic bulk Update command is available for workflows, but workflow.updateMany has a pre-query hook that unconditionally throws Method not allowed, so every offered bulk rename fails.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The Workflows list offers and confirms bulk Name updates, but submitting them always returns “Method not allowed” and leaves the selected workflows unchanged.

sourceBugs.name: Bulk workflow Name update is offered but always fails with Method not allowed

reproductionPaths.expected: The Workflows list should not offer and confirm a bulk Name update that is unconditionally unsupported. An offered, confirmed update should complete, or the unsupported action should be unavailable.
reproductionPaths.actual: Selecting two workflows, entering a replacement Name, and confirming Update records closes the confirmation and shows “Method not allowed.” Both original names remain unchanged after refresh, although individual workflow renaming succeeds.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and open Workflows.
Create two draft workflows with distinct, uniquely prefixed names, then return to the Workflows list.
Select both workflow rows and click Update.
Enter a replacement Name in Update records, click Apply, and confirm Update 2 records.
Observe the “Method not allowed” error and unchanged workflow names. Refresh the list and confirm the original names remain.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dragging an Active workflow version into Deactivated is rejected, but the board leaves the card in Deactivated with a false status until navigation or refresh.

rootCause.explanation: Board dragging optimistically changes per-column record-ID membership before issuing the update. Workflow version/run hooks reject status writes, and rollback restores record fields without restoring those independent column memberships.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Dragging an Active workflow version into Deactivated is rejected, but the board leaves the card in Deactivated with a false status until navigation or refresh.

sourceBugs.name: Rejected workflow version status drag leaves the card falsely displayed as Deactivated

reproductionPaths.expected: After rejecting a workflow version status change, the board should keep or restore the card and its status badge to the saved Active state.
reproductionPaths.actual: A toast says “This field cannot be updated directly on a workflow version,” yet the card remains in the Deactivated column and displays Deactivated. The saved version is still Active; opening its record or refreshing the board restores the correct display.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and open Workflows.
Create a uniquely named workflow, add a Launch manually trigger and a Delay action, then activate it.
Open Workflow Versions and create a uniquely named Kanban view grouped by Version status.
Filter the view to the new workflow, save the view, and reload the board. Verify the version card appears as Active.
Drag the Active version card into the Deactivated column.
Observe the rejection toast while the card remains in Deactivated with a Deactivated badge. Refresh the board and verify the card returns to Active.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A forbidden Workflow Run status change is rejected by the server, but Kanban retains the optimistic column placement until reload.

sourceBugs.name: Rejected Workflow Run status drag leaves the card in the destination column

reproductionPaths.expected: After a rejected status drag, the run card should return to its saved status column.
reproductionPaths.actual: Dragging a Failed workflow run into Completed displays a permission error, but the card remains under Completed. Its badge can disagree with the column or retain the optimistic label. Reload returns the card to Failed; the stored status was not changed.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow that produces two Failed runs. Open Workflow Runs in a Kanban view grouped by run status.
Drag one owned Failed run into Completed and wait for the permission error.
Observe the card remains in Completed after the rejection and a settled wait. Repeat with the second failed run.
Reload and confirm both return to Failed. Compare an allowed Opportunity stage drag, which saves and remains in its destination after reload.

guidance.distinction: This entry covers Workflow Runs and its run-update permission rejection. N04 covers Workflow Versions and its distinct version-status rejection. Do not match an actual saved status change, delayed execution, or a rejected delete banner.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers Workflow Runs and its run-update permission rejection. N04 covers Workflow Versions and its distinct version-status rejection. Do not match an actual saved status change, delayed execution, or a rejected delete banner.

limitations: Joint scope is Workflow Runs Kanban status-column placement after a rejected Failed-to-Completed drag. No persisted run-status change or execution failure is claimed.
The badge varies between attempts and may show Failed or the optimistic destination status; the stable defect is placement in the wrong column.
Both reviewers used two failed runs in one owned workflow, rather than two independently constructed workflows.
Exact cache/mount ordering is inferred. Newer source adds drag restrictions to some dashboard and record-page relation widgets; no newer-runtime result is claimed.
Same-column reorder, other destinations, grouped-table/calendar callers and broader object behavior are excluded.

logicalBugs.explanation: Leaving the Iterator settings panel within its one-second save delay silently discards pending input edits, including an input-array selection or deletion of a literal item. A lost array selection can make the workflow complete without processing the intended loop.

rootCause.explanation: Iterator settings use a 1000ms debounced saveAction while updating local formData immediately; closing/switching the panel before it fires unmounts that owner without flushing pending edits.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Leaving the Iterator settings panel within its one-second save delay silently discards pending input edits, including an input-array selection or deletion of a literal item. A lost array selection can make the workflow complete without processing the intended loop.

sourceBugs.name: Iterator silently loses pending edits when its settings panel is closed or changed quickly

reproductionPaths.expected: Iterator settings edited through the editor should persist when the user closes the panel or moves to another step, including pending array selections and literal-item deletions within the save delay.
reproductionPaths.actual: The All Companies array chip appears immediately after selection, but closing the panel or switching steps within about one second prevents the edit from saving. Reopening after refresh shows an empty Items input. Waiting longer than the save delay retains the selection. In a tested workflow, the lost input caused a completed run to skip the loop Delay despite Search Records returning two companies; restoring the input and waiting made Delay execute twice. In a separate literal-array reproduction, deleting Alpha from saved Alpha/Beta shows only Beta, but immediately switching to another step and returning restores both items without a save request. Waiting for the deletion to save before leaving retains only Beta through navigation and refresh.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and create a uniquely named workflow with a Launch manually trigger.
Add Search Records for Companies with Limit 2, then add an Iterator.
In the Iterator Items input, select Search Records > All Companies from the variable picker.
Immediately close the Iterator settings panel or select its loop step, within about one second of choosing the array.
Wait, refresh the page, reopen the Iterator, and observe the empty Items input instead of the selected All Companies chip.
As a control, select All Companies again, wait at least two seconds before leaving the panel, and refresh. The selection persists.

Alternate reproduction: configure and save literal Iterator items Alpha and Beta, then reload to verify both. Delete Alpha and immediately select another workflow step within the one-second save delay. Return to the Iterator and observe Alpha restored. Repeat the deletion but wait at least two seconds before switching steps; only Beta remains after navigation and refresh.

logicalBugs.explanation: Discarding a workflow draft leaves an already-open Create Record editor showing discarded values. Editing another field spreads those stale values into a new draft, which can execute the discarded title or other mapping.

rootCause.explanation: WorkflowEditActionCreateRecord initializes formData from action.settings.input once and does not synchronize that local object when discard replaces the displayed version. Its next field update spreads the stale formData into the replacement draft. This confirmed local-state cause is separate from the Delay override report, whose editor has an explicit input synchronization effect.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Discarding a workflow draft leaves its open settings panel showing discarded values. Editing another field can save those stale values into a new draft and execute them.

sourceBugs.name: Discard Draft leaves stale settings that a later edit saves into a new workflow draft

reproductionPaths.expected: Discard Draft should delete the unpublished workflow version and return the editor to the active configuration. An open settings panel should close or refresh to that configuration, and subsequent edits should not silently restore discarded values.
reproductionPaths.actual: After discarding a draft whose Create Record action has Title Original, the canvas returns to Active but the open action panel still shows Original instead of the active Title Updated. Test without another edit creates Updated, and reopening the panel corrects its display. Editing only Body in the stale panel instead creates a new draft that restores Title Original; testing that new draft creates a Note with the discarded title.
reproSteps: Use a wide desktop viewport so Discard Draft is available in the workflow header without replacing the open settings panel.
Create a uniquely named workflow with Launch manually and Create Record > Notes, set Title to Original, and activate v1.
Edit the action Title to Updated and activate v2, leaving v1 archived.
Open archived v1 in Workflow Versions and choose Use as Draft.
Open the draft Create Record action settings, verify Title Original, and leave the panel open.
Click the header Discard Draft. Observe that the canvas shows Active while the panel still displays Original.
Without closing or reopening the panel, edit only Body and wait for the edit to save. Observe a new draft with the discarded Title Original restored.
Test the new draft and inspect the created Note: its Title is Original, although the only post-discard edit was to Body.

logicalBugs.explanation: Overriding an existing workflow draft from another version can leave the reopened Delay editor showing the discarded draft duration. Editing only a different duration field writes the old duration back into the replacement draft and persists it after reload.

rootCause.explanation: Override Draft replaces persisted version content, but the returned editor can still supply the previous draft action snapshot to Delay. WorkflowEditActionDelay initializes from action.settings.input and explicitly resynchronizes localDuration whenever those duration props change, so an absence of local synchronization is ruled out. The stale snapshot must precede that input boundary; the precise override/navigation/cache ordering is not established by the available evidence.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Use as Draft followed by Override Draft correctly replaces an existing draft on the server, but the editor retains the old draft settings and later writes them back when another field is edited.

sourceBugs.name: Override Draft leaves stale settings that a later edit saves over restored values

reproductionPaths.expected: After overriding the current draft with a selected historical version, the editor should show that restored version’s values and subsequent edits should preserve its other restored settings.
reproductionPaths.actual: A selected version has Delay Seconds 1 and the old draft has Seconds 2. Override Draft restores 1 server-side, but reopening Delay in the returned editor still shows 2. Editing only another duration field saves the stale Seconds 2 back, and the unintended value persists after reload.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create a fresh workflow with Launch manually and a Delay of 1 second. Activate it as the first version.
Edit that workflow’s Delay to 2 seconds to create a newer draft. Wait for saving to complete and load the edited draft in the editor.
Open version history and select the first version, verifying that its Delay is still 1 second.
Choose Use as Draft and confirm Override Draft when told a draft already exists.
In the returned draft editor, reopen Delay. Observe that Seconds still displays the old draft value 2 rather than restored value 1.
Without changing Seconds, change Minutes to 1 and allow saving to complete. Reload and reopen Delay; observe that Seconds 2 has been saved back along with the intentional Minutes edit.

As a control, fully reload immediately after Override Draft before editing any field; the restored 1-second setting displays correctly. Use as Draft without an existing draft also displays the copied settings correctly.

logicalBugs.explanation: A rejected Delete on a workflow run or version leaves its detail page falsely displaying a deleted record and Restore controls, although the record remains undeleted.

rootCause.explanation: Generic record deletion optimistically sets deletedAt and deleted-record presentation before a request that workflow run/version pre-query hooks reject. Some record-show state remains in the deleted view even after the field rollback.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A rejected Delete on a workflow run or version leaves its detail page falsely displaying a deleted record and Restore controls, although the record remains undeleted.

sourceBugs.name: Rejected workflow run or version deletion leaves a false deleted banner and Restore controls

reproductionPaths.expected: When deletion is rejected, the detail page should retain or restore the undeleted presentation, without a deleted banner or Restore controls.
reproductionPaths.actual: Delete Workflow Run or Delete Workflow Version shows “You do not have permission to perform this workflow action,” but the detail page also shows “This record has been deleted” and Restore controls. Refresh clears the false deleted presentation and retains the same undeleted record. No persisted deletion or data loss was observed.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and create a uniquely named manual workflow with a Form containing a Text field.
Test the workflow, leave the Form pending, and open the full run detail from Workflow Runs. Close the Form panel if it opens.
Open the run Command Menu and choose Delete Workflow Run.
Observe the permission-denied toast together with the false deleted banner and Restore controls.
Refresh the detail page. Verify the deleted banner disappears and the same undeleted run remains.

For the version variant, create and activate a manual workflow with Delay 1 second, change Delay to 2 seconds and activate v2, then open archived v1 and choose Delete Workflow Version. The rejected deletion produces the same false state, which clears on refresh.

logicalBugs.explanation: See Runs on a workflow version drops the selected version scope and shows runs from other versions. After a fresh version-page load it can also omit workflow scope and show unrelated workflows’ runs.

rootCause.explanation: SeeRunsWorkflowVersion builds its second filter under recordStore instead of the WorkflowRun workflowVersion relation. The navigation filter cannot apply the selected version.

reproductionPaths.explanation: See Runs on a workflow version drops the selected version scope and shows runs from other versions. After a fresh version-page load it can also omit workflow scope and show unrelated workflows’ runs.

sourceBugs.name: Workflow Version See Runs omits the selected version filter

reproductionPaths.expected: See Runs from a specific workflow version should show only runs linked to that version. An untested v2 should show an empty run list rather than runs from v1.
reproductionPaths.actual: On two fresh workflows, v2 had an empty Runs relation but See Runs displayed the completed run from v1 with only a Workflow filter. Opening that run confirmed Workflow version v1. A manually applied v2 filter correctly returned no runs. Freshly loading a version page before See Runs also produced an unscoped workspace run list containing unrelated workflows.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and create a uniquely named workflow with Launch manually and a Delay action set to 1 second.
Test the draft once to create a completed v1 run, then activate v1.
Change Delay to 2 seconds and activate the resulting v2 without testing it.
Open Workflow Versions, open this workflow’s v2, and verify its Runs relation is empty.
Click See Runs. Observe the v1 run appears; open it and verify its Workflow version is v1.
As a control, manually filter Workflow Runs by this workflow and its exact v2. The list correctly has no runs.
For the missing-workflow-scope variant, refresh a version detail page and then click See Runs. Observe that the resulting list can also include unrelated workflows’ runs.

logicalBugs.explanation: Restoring a deleted draft workflow leaves its stored Statuses empty, so its table status is blank and Draft filtering excludes it even though the editor still shows Draft.

rootCause.explanation: Workflow lifecycle restore undeletes child versions but does not rebuild the parent denormalized statuses from the restored draft, leaving the restored draft workflow outside Draft-filtered lists.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Restoring a deleted draft workflow leaves its stored Statuses empty, so its table status is blank and Draft filtering excludes it even though the editor still shows Draft.

sourceBugs.name: Restored draft workflows lose their list status and disappear from Draft filters

reproductionPaths.expected: Restored draft workflows should show Draft in the Workflows Statuses column and remain included when the list is filtered to Draft.
reproductionPaths.actual: Restored workflows have blank Statuses cells after refresh, while their editors still show Draft and retain their workflow configuration. A Statuses: Draft filter excludes the restored drafts and retains the otherwise equivalent undeleted control. The restored versions are Draft but the parent workflow’s saved statuses array is empty.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and create two uniquely named draft workflows with manual triggers and an action.
Create or use an isolated Workflows table view filtered to those workflows. Verify both initially show Draft in Statuses.
Select both rows and use the table context menu to Delete Workflows.
Open the command menu and choose See deleted Workflows. Select the two deleted workflows, choose Restore Workflows, and confirm.
Remove the Deleted filter and reload the Workflows table. Observe both restored rows have blank Statuses cells.
Open a restored workflow and verify its editor still shows Draft and its configuration remains.
Return to the table and apply Statuses: Draft. Observe the restored drafts are excluded; an equivalent draft that was never deleted remains included.

logicalBugs.explanation: Discard Draft retains the completed draft test run, but its Flow becomes Invalid Configuration and its step-output inspection stops working.

rootCause.explanation: Discard soft-deletes the draft WorkflowVersion; historical run inspection still asks the standard version-content query for that deleted version instead of consistently using the saved run.state.flow snapshot.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Discard Draft retains the completed draft test run, but its Flow becomes Invalid Configuration and its step-output inspection stops working.

sourceBugs.name: Discarding a tested workflow draft breaks its completed run Flow and output inspection

reproductionPaths.expected: A retained completed run should remain inspectable after its draft is discarded, including the executed Flow and step outputs stored with that run.
reproductionPaths.actual: Before discard, the completed draft test run shows successful Trigger and Delay nodes and inspectable Delay output. After Discard Draft, reopening the same run still shows Completed but its Flow shows only Invalid Configuration, the version relation is empty, and step-output controls are unavailable. The failure persists after reload. See Version reports an error without navigating. The saved execution snapshot and results remain visible in State; no loss of execution data was observed.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and create a uniquely named workflow with Launch manually and Create Record > Notes using a unique Note title.
Test the workflow successfully, then activate v1.
Edit the active workflow by replacing Create Record with a Delay action set to 2 seconds, leaving the other time units zero.
Test this draft and open its completed run. Verify the Flow shows successful Trigger and Delay nodes and the Delay output is inspectable.
Close the run panel and click Discard Draft to return the workflow to its active Create Record version.
Open See Runs and reopen the same completed Delay test run, then use Open for its full detail.
Observe Completed alongside Invalid Configuration in Flow, an empty version relation and missing step-output controls. Refresh and verify the Flow remains broken.
Click See Version and observe the error without navigation. As a control, reopen a run of retained v1 and verify its Flow and outputs still work.

logicalBugs.explanation: An unconfigured or no-longer-eligible Select value is displayed as the first available option without saving that choice. Workflow Form sources, Form answers, action mappings and time zones can therefore look configured but submit no value; role selectors can display a different role from the saved assignment. A sole unsaved option can also be disabled, preventing explicit selection.

rootCause.explanation: Select derives selectedOption by matching value, then falls back to options[0] when no emptyOption is supplied. This fallback neither changes the stored value nor calls onChange. Its single-option disabled condition additionally treats the visually selected fallback as a real selection. Workflow and role callers pass unset or filtered-out values into this shared behavior.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A new Create Calendar Event action displays American Samoa as its selected time zone although its configured time zone is empty.

sourceBugs.name: Unset Create Calendar Event time zone falsely displays American Samoa as selected

reproductionPaths.expected: When no time zone is configured, the Time zone selector should show an empty or explicit no-selection state instead of a specific zone that is not stored.
reproductionPaths.actual: Before any time zone is selected on a fresh Create Calendar Event action, the Time zone field displays “(GMT-11:00) American Samoa Standard Time.” The step’s stored time zone is empty. Explicitly selecting New York and allowing autosave to finish persists correctly; completed-save reversion and calendar execution failure are not part of this finding.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and create a uniquely named draft workflow with a Launch manually trigger.
Add a Create Calendar Event action and open its configuration panel.
Before choosing a time zone, inspect Time zone: American Samoa is displayed as selected despite no zone having been configured.
As a control, explicitly select New York, allow autosave to finish, then close and reopen the panel or refresh. New York remains selected.
Do not execute the calendar action; the demonstrated defect is the false empty-value display.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A workflow Form Select based on Opportunity Stage displays New as selected even when no value is set. Submitting it untouched completes without a Stage answer, while explicitly selecting the same New option submits NEW.

sourceBugs.name: Workflow Form Select shows New as selected but omits it from submitted answers

reproductionPaths.expected: A submitted Form should include the answer displayed as selected. If the field has no answer, it should present a clear empty state instead of displaying and checkmarking New as selected.
reproductionPaths.actual: The runtime Form shows New in Stage and marks New selected in the open dropdown. Submitting without choosing an option completes with an empty result. Explicitly clicking the already checkmarked New and submitting returns the corresponding NEW value. The omission reproduces in Test and when launching an activated workflow through the Command Menu; saved and submitted values are not lost through refresh or save interruption.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create an owned workflow with a Launch manually trigger and a Form action.

Add a Select input, give it a unique label such as Sales status, and explicitly choose Existing field > Opportunity > Stage as its source field. Do not set a default answer. Allow configuration saving to complete.
Run Test. Observe that the Stage dropdown already displays New. Open the dropdown and observe New is checkmarked; dismiss it without selecting an option.
Click Submit. After the run completes, open the Form step Output and observe an empty result with no Sales status answer.
Run the same form again, explicitly click New in the dropdown, then Submit. Observe the completed output contains salesStatus: NEW.
Activate the valid workflow and launch it through the Command Menu. Leave the displayed New untouched and Submit; the completed Form result is again empty.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Selecting Stage under Fields to update displays New without storing a stage value in objectRecord. The saved action contains the edited Name only. Explicitly selecting New stores stage NEW correctly.

sourceBugs.name: Update Record editor misleadingly displays an unsaved Stage=New value

reproductionPaths.expected: The Update Record editor should distinguish an unset Stage from an explicitly configured New value.
reproductionPaths.actual: Selecting Stage under Fields to update displays New without storing a stage value in objectRecord. The saved action contains the edited Name only. Explicitly selecting New stores stage NEW correctly.
reproSteps: Create a workflow with an Opportunity Update Record action and select Stage and Name under Fields to update.
Leave the displayed Stage New untouched and enter a valid Name. Allow saving to complete.
Inspect the displayed Stage and saved action configuration. Stage appears New, but objectRecord contains the Name without a stage value.
Explicitly select New and compare the saved configuration, which now contains stage NEW.

guidance.distinction: This entry displays an unsaved Opportunity Stage default in Update Record; N53 covers Create Record Task Status defaults and explicit No Status.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry displays an unsaved Opportunity Stage default in Update Record; N53 covers Create Record Task Status defaults and explicit No Status.

limitations: Approval is limited to misleading editor presentation. Explicitly selected New saves correctly; no backend refusal of a saved NEW value or fresh downstream execution damage is claimed.
Evidence basis: fresh UI + source.
No independent Claude agreement or newer-runtime verification is claimed.
Targeted UI tool captures, screenshots and source were audited. The Codex batch was stopped after useful checks; this does not represent a completed formal judge verdict.

reproductionPaths.explanation: New Form Select and Multi-Select fields display an existing source as selected without saving its source ID. With only one Multi-Select source available, the picker disables itself, preventing configuration and causing the entire input to be omitted at runtime.

sourceBugs.name: Workflow Form source picker shows an unsaved selection and blocks the sole Multi-Select source

reproductionPaths.expected: A source shown as selected should be stored, or the source picker should clearly require and permit an explicit selection, including when only one source is available. A Form input should become usable after choosing a supported existing field.
reproductionPaths.actual: The builder displays Opportunity > Stage for Select and Workflow > Statuses for Multi-Select, but saved settings have no selectedFieldId. Runtime forms omit these inputs while ordinary Number and Date fields render. Explicitly selecting a source repairs Select. The sole Multi-Select source picker is disabled and cannot make that selection, so Multi-Select remains absent after saving, reload, Test, and an activated workflow launch. The existing source already defines its answer options; no separate Form options-entry step is missing.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator in the fixture workspace, where Workflow > Statuses is the only available Multi-Select source. Create an owned manual workflow with a Form action.

Add a Number field, a uniquely named Select field, and a uniquely named Multi-Select field. Open each choice field settings and observe that its Field source displays Opportunity > Stage or Workflow > Statuses without explicitly selecting it.
For Multi-Select, attempt to open the Field source picker. Observe it is disabled despite the source selection not being saved. The source already has Draft, Active, and Deactivated answer options.
Allow the configuration to save, reload, and run Test. Observe that the form contains Number but omits the entire Select and Multi-Select inputs.

As a control, return to the Select settings and explicitly choose Opportunity > Stage or Task > Status. Save, reload, and Test; that Select now renders. Multi-Select remains absent because its sole source cannot be selected.
The omission can also be observed when the workflow is activated and launched through the Command Menu.

logicalBugs.explanation: Choosing POST when the webhook method is already POST overwrites a saved custom Expected Body with defaults, while the editor continues displaying the old JSON.

rootCause.explanation: HTTP method onChange replaces settings with getWebhookTriggerDefaultSettings even when POST is reselected. Expected Body is reset, while the mounted JSON editor retains its previously initialized text.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Choosing POST when the webhook method is already POST overwrites a saved custom Expected Body with defaults, while the editor continues displaying the old JSON.

sourceBugs.name: Re-selecting POST silently resets the saved webhook Expected Body while showing stale JSON

reproductionPaths.expected: Selecting the already-selected HTTP method should preserve the saved webhook configuration. The Expected Body editor should accurately reflect the configuration being saved.
reproductionPaths.actual: A custom Expected Body survives a normal reload, but re-selecting the checkmarked POST option saves the default {"message":"Workflow was started"} instead. The editor temporarily retains the custom JSON, concealing the overwrite. Reopening the panel or refreshing reveals the default body. The method remains POST and no warning appears.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and create a uniquely named draft workflow with a Webhook trigger and a Delay action.
Select POST, replace Expected Body with a valid custom JSON object such as {"custom":"retained","count":2}, then blur the editor and allow the save to finish.
Refresh and reopen the trigger to verify the custom body is saved and POST is selected.
Open the HTTP method dropdown and click POST again, even though it is already checkmarked.
Observe that the Expected Body editor still displays the custom JSON.
Close and reopen the trigger panel or refresh. Observe that Expected Body has been overwritten with {"message":"Workflow was started"} while the method remains POST.
As a control, save the custom body again, open the method menu and dismiss it without choosing an option. Refresh and verify the custom body remains.

logicalBugs.explanation: Selecting a workflow in a freshly loaded Workflows list and clicking See Runs can open the unfiltered workspace run list, including runs from unrelated workflows.

rootCause.explanation: SeeRuns derives its workflow filter from asynchronous useWorkflowWithCurrentVersion rather than the already selected recordId. Initial render can navigate with an undefined selected workflow ID.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Selecting a workflow in a freshly loaded Workflows list and clicking See Runs can open the unfiltered workspace run list, including runs from unrelated workflows.

sourceBugs.name: See Runs from a freshly loaded Workflows selection loses the selected workflow filter

reproductionPaths.expected: See Runs for a selected workflow should show only that workflow’s runs. The action should not silently ignore selected workflows; if it supports only one workflow, it should be unavailable for multiple selections.
reproductionPaths.actual: After freshly loading the Workflows list, selecting one workflow and clicking See Runs navigates to Workflow Runs without a Workflow filter, showing runs from unrelated workflows. Opening the workflow record first allows the single-selection shortcut to filter correctly. With two workflows selected, the offered action can show all runs or filter only the first selected workflow.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user. Create two uniquely named workflows A and B with Launch manually and a one-second Delay; test each to create a completed run.
Return to Workflows and reload the list. Do not open either workflow record before using the list action.
Select only A using its row checkbox, then click the header See Runs action.
Observe that Workflow Runs has no Workflow filter and includes B or other unrelated workflows’ runs.
Repeat from a freshly loaded Workflows list with B selected alone to verify the same missing scope.
As a control, open A’s workflow record first, return to the list, select A and click See Runs. The resulting list correctly filters to A.

For the multiple-selection variant, select A and B in the list and use the offered See Runs action. Observe that it can omit workflow filtering or show only the first selected workflow rather than respecting the selection.

logicalBugs.explanation: Workflow variable expressions cannot reliably reference literal object keys containing dots or slashes. Picker-selected values can resolve a different nested property or no value, producing incorrect action inputs.

rootCause.explanation: Workflow variable expressions encode object property names as dot/slash-delimited paths without an escaping scheme. Literal dotted or slash-containing keys are parsed as path structure and resolve to nested data or no value.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The webhook variable picker separately offers a literal customer.name key, but selecting it maps the nested customer > name field and creates a Note with the wrong title.

sourceBugs.name: Selecting a literal dotted webhook key writes the nested field value instead

reproductionPaths.expected: Selecting the offered top-level customer.name field should use its previewed value, distinct from the nested customer > name field. An unsupported key should not silently substitute another field’s value.
reproductionPaths.actual: With different sample values for the literal customer.name key and nested customer.name, the picker offers the literal key with the Dotted preview. Selecting it inserts a chip labeled name with a Webhook > customer > name path. Test completes and creates a Note titled Nested rather than Dotted, although both distinct input values remain present in the sample.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user and create a uniquely named workflow with a Webhook trigger.
Choose POST and set Expected Body to {"customer.name":"Dotted sample","customer":{"name":"Nested sample"},"plain":"Plain sample"}. Blur the JSON editor and allow the configuration to save.
Add a Create Record action with Object Notes.
Open the Title variable picker and select the top-level customer.name option previewing Dotted sample, rather than the customer submenu’s name field.
Observe that the inserted chip is labeled name and identifies the nested Webhook > customer > name path.
Click Test, wait for Completed, and inspect the Create Record output and created Note. Its Title is Nested sample rather than the selected Dotted sample.
As controls, deliberately select nested customer > name and then plain in separate tests. Those selections produce Nested sample and Plain sample respectively.
Use the Expected Body sample through Test; no live webhook delivery is required.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The variable picker offers a nonempty webhook field named a/b, but mapping it to Create Record Notes Body creates a saved Note with no selected content.

sourceBugs.name: Selecting a slash-named webhook field creates a Note with a blank body

reproductionPaths.expected: Selecting the offered literal webhook field a/b should insert its displayed value into the created Note body.
reproductionPaths.actual: The picker previews the nonempty a/b value and saves the mapping chip. The completed run retains that value in its trigger data, but Create Record stores a blank Note body. Opening the created Note independently confirms the content is missing.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create a fresh workflow with a POST webhook trigger.

logicalBugs.explanation: Changing a database trigger to another object preserves incompatible old conditions and monitored fields. Pickers can show the former object schema, and activation or execution can retain conditions that do not belong to the new object.

rootCause.explanation: Changing the database trigger object updates eventName while preserving old filter and monitored-field settings. Pickers/cache can retain the former schema or hide unresolved names, and activation does not reject references incompatible with the new object.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Changing a record trigger from Workflows to Companies leaves existing Conditions field pickers offering Workflow fields and prevents selecting Company fields until the panel is reopened.

sourceBugs.name: Changing trigger Record Type leaves existing condition pickers on the previous object

reproductionPaths.expected: After Record Type changes, existing Conditions pickers should offer fields of the newly selected object, without requiring the trigger panel to be reopened.
reproductionPaths.actual: After changing Record Type from Workflows to Companies, an existing condition picker still displays Workflow · Pick a Workflow record and Workflow fields such as Statuses and Core workflow id. Company-only fields such as Domain Name are unavailable. A newly added rule or reopening the trigger panel correctly shows Company fields.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture Admin user, create a uniquely named workflow and add a Record is created trigger.
Add a Conditions filter row and set Record Type to Workflows.
Allow the configuration to save, refresh and reopen the trigger. Verify the condition field picker shows Workflow fields, then dismiss the picker while leaving the trigger panel open.
Change Record Type from Workflows to Companies and allow the change to save without closing the trigger panel.
Open Select a field in the existing Conditions row. Observe that it still shows Workflow and its fields rather than Company fields; Company-only Domain fields cannot be selected.
As controls, add a new condition rule and observe its picker correctly shows Company fields, or close and reopen the trigger panel and observe the existing picker is corrected.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Changing a Record-updated trigger from Notes to Companies retains the old Title condition after reload; it displays Select a field and the active workflow does not run on Company updates.

sourceBugs.name: Changing trigger Record Type retains an incompatible condition that prevents runs

reproductionPaths.expected: After changing the trigger object, incompatible object-specific conditions should be reset or clearly identified as invalid so a retained old-object condition does not silently prevent execution.
reproductionPaths.actual: Notes Title Contains a nonempty value survives switching to Companies as a saved trigger.properties.after.title reference. The field displays Select a field, activation succeeds, and Company updates produce no run. Selecting a valid Company Name condition restores normal execution.
reproSteps: Create a fresh workflow with Record is updated > Notes. Add a Title Contains condition with a unique nonempty value.
Change Record Type to Companies, directly or through Tasks. Observe Select a field while Contains and the previous value remain.
Add a harmless valid action, allow saving to finish, and activate. Reload and confirm the unresolved field remains.
Update an owned Company and observe no run for the stale condition.
As a control, explicitly select Company Name in that condition and use a value matching the Company. Save and activate, update the Company again, and observe a completed run.

guidance.distinction: N17 covers stale current-object picker options after Record Type changes, recoverable by reopening the panel. This entry covers a saved old-object condition whose field remains unresolved after reopening/reload and prevents matching runs; explicit reselection repairs it.

matchingGuidance.distinction: N17 covers stale current-object picker options after Record Type changes, recoverable by reopening the panel. The precise listener cause of absent runs was inferred from source, not traced live. No HTTP Request was executed; harmless actions were used.
An additional displayed-versus-saved operand discrepancy is uninvestigated and excluded.
Latest was source-inspected only; the later malformed-template warning is a different cause.

sourceBugs.name: Changing a database trigger object conceals retained monitored fields and prevents runs

reproductionPaths.expected: The optional monitored-fields selector should accurately display its saved restrictions after an object change, or clear incompatible restrictions before activation. A visibly unrestricted trigger should behave like the working no-field-restriction control.
reproductionPaths.actual: After selecting Companies Annual Revenue and switching to People, the Fields selector shows its empty placeholder after reload, but saved settings retain annualRevenue. Activation succeeds, and saved Person name changes produce no new run. Clearing the retained restriction restores execution. A truly unrestricted People trigger looks the same and runs normally.

As a control, configure a fresh People trigger without selected fields and verify the same name edits start it.
For recovery, switch the affected trigger back to Companies, uncheck the retained field, return to People and activate. Verify a later name edit starts a run.

logicalBugs.explanation: HTTP Request actions receiving an HTTP 404 or 500 response can be saved as successful steps and mark the workflow Completed; later actions execute even with Continue on failure disabled.

rootCause.explanation: HttpTool catches HTTP failures and returns an object containing error/status rather than throwing. The workflow action/executor interprets the resolved result as successful and schedules following steps.

reproductionPaths.explanation: HTTP Request actions receiving an HTTP 404 or 500 response can be saved as successful steps and mark the workflow Completed; later actions execute even with Continue on failure disabled.

sourceBugs.name: HTTP errors are marked successful and let workflow execution continue

reproductionPaths.expected: With Continue on failure disabled, an HTTP error reported as Request Failed by action Test should fail the workflow action and run rather than be recorded as successful and execute subsequent actions.
reproductionPaths.actual: Action Test reports Request Failed for a 404, but the same request in a full workflow run is recorded as SUCCESS and the run is Completed while its logs retain HTTP 404 NOT FOUND. A 500 response is also marked successful. A following action executes despite Continue on failure being off.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator, create a fresh workflow and add a Launch manually trigger.
Add an HTTP Request action with method POST, URL https://httpbin.org/status/404 and raw JSON body {}. Leave Continue on failure disabled and allow the configuration to save.
Test the HTTP action and observe Request Failed with status code 404.
Run Test Workflow. Inspect its Completed status, successful HTTP action and Logs containing 404 NOT FOUND.

For the continuation variant, add a following HTTP Request to https://httpbin.org/status/200, save and test the workflow again. Observe that the following action executes despite the preceding HTTP error and disabled Continue on failure.
As controls, changing the failing endpoint to a 200 response makes action Test and the workflow agree on success, while an unreachable-host request fails the workflow normally.

logicalBugs.explanation: Alphabetical and Reverse Alphabetical group ordering works immediately in grouped Table and Kanban views but resets to Manual after reload, including Opportunity Stage, Task Status and Workflow Runs views.

rootCause.explanation: The group-order menu updates an in-memory component state defaulting to Manual. Column ordering reads it, but view persistence and loading omit that setting. Neighboring visibility settings use stored view fields.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Reverse Alphabetical group ordering in a custom Workflow Runs view resets to Manual after refresh, even after an explicit Update view save completes.

sourceBugs.name: Workflow Runs group sort resets to Manual after refreshing a saved view

reproductionPaths.expected: A saved custom view should retain the chosen group ordering after refresh, consistently with its saved grouping, filters and Hide empty groups setting.
reproductionPaths.actual: Selecting Reverse Alphabetical immediately changes the group order, but refreshing restores Manual and the previous display order. Completed Update view saves preserve other configuration without preserving group sort.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create or use owned workflows with runs in at least two statuses, such as Completed and Failed.
Open Workflow Runs and create a fresh custom table view. Group by run status and optionally hide empty groups.
In Options > Group > Sort choose Reverse Alphabetical. Confirm that Failed appears before Completed.
Change a saved filter or record sort to enable Update view, click Update view and wait for the save to finish.
Refresh and reopen the same view. Observe that group Sort now reads Manual and the chosen group ordering is lost, while the other saved view settings persist.
As controls, reapply Reverse Alphabetical to restore the order, or navigate within the app and return without a full reload to observe that the in-memory selection remains.

logicalBugs.explanation: Record-list header counts and grouped Table calculations can omit active search, explicit filters or group conditions. Totals and sums can include rows excluded from the displayed results, and filtered-out groups can retain calculations from their hidden records.

rootCause.explanation: Table footer and header aggregate hooks combine independently compiled filters using object spread. Group, explicit filters and any-field search can each contain top-level and/or keys; later objects replace earlier predicates rather than conjoining them, so summaries include records excluded by the row query.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A custom Workflow Runs table grouped by Workflow or Workflow version with no configured groups displays matching run rows but reports a total count of zero.

sourceBugs.name: Workflow Runs counter reports zero while matching runs remain visible

reproductionPaths.expected: The live run count and visible rows in the same filtered view should describe the same collection.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Workflow or Workflow version grouping selected and no manually configured groups, the table displays matching runs as flat rows while its live counter shows 0. Completed saves, reload and ordinary navigation retain the inconsistency. Adding the matching groups manually makes the rows and count agree.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create two owned manual workflows with valid actions. Run them to produce several identifiable Workflow Runs.
Open Workflow Runs, create a fresh custom table view and apply a filter that includes the owned runs. Confirm matching rows are present.
Choose Options > Group > Workflow without adding any manual relation groups. Allow the configuration to save.
Observe that matching runs remain visible as flat rows while the view counter reports 0. Refresh or navigate away and return to confirm the inconsistency persists.
Repeat with Group by Workflow version and no manually configured groups.
As controls, group by run status or manually add the matching Workflow groups through Options > New group; observe matching rows and a correct count.

logicalBugs.explanation: After changing a tested draft’s webhook sample schema, opening its earlier successful run through in-app navigation falsely labels an original valid mapping Not Found.

rootCause.explanation: Historical run variable labels are resolved against current editable workflow steps/output schema rather than the run saved flow snapshot. Renamed/deleted steps in the current version make valid historical references appear Not Found.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After changing a tested draft’s webhook sample schema, opening its earlier successful run through in-app navigation falsely labels an original valid mapping Not Found.

sourceBugs.name: Historical workflow run falsely marks its original variable mapping Not Found

reproductionPaths.expected: The read-only Node inspector for a historical run should resolve its mappings against that run’s saved flow and schema, consistently with its original Input and Output.
reproductionPaths.actual: The historical run’s Node tab shows Not Found for its original Body mapping after the current draft schema changes, while the same run’s stored input still contains the original field and its output retains the correct Note content. A full reload of the run page restores the correct mapping label.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create a fresh POST webhook workflow with Expected Body {"customer":{"name":"Example","address":{"city":"Paris"}}}.
Add Create Record for Notes, map Title to customer.name and Body to customer.address.city, and wait for saving to finish.
Test the workflow successfully and keep the first run. Verify its trigger Input contains city Paris, its created Note Body contains Paris, and its Node tab resolves the city mapping.
Return to the draft and replace the webhook sample with {"customer":{"name":"Updated"},"zip":"69000"}. Wait for saving to finish; another test run is unnecessary.
Without reloading the page, use See Runs to open the first run, select Create Record and open its Node tab. Observe that its original mapping is now labelled Not Found.

Inspect that historical run’s Input and Output to confirm the original city value and created Note content remain correct. Fully reload the same run page and observe the correct mapping label returns.

logicalBugs.explanation: Webhook Test replaces nonempty sample fields named payload and metadata with internal trigger context, so picker-selected values create Notes with blank or incorrect content.

rootCause.explanation: Webhook test payload construction merges test metadata and supplied expected body with conflicting reserved keys, overwriting user-provided payload/metadata values rather than namespacing the synthetic fields.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Webhook Test replaces nonempty sample fields named payload and metadata with internal trigger context, so picker-selected values create Notes with blank or incorrect content.

sourceBugs.name: Webhook Test overwrites supplied payload and metadata fields

reproductionPaths.expected: POST webhook Test should resolve picker-selected fields to the values supplied in Expected Body, consistently with the field structure delivered through the live webhook.
reproductionPaths.actual: The picker previews nonempty payload.id and metadata.label values, but completed Test runs create Notes with blank titles and bodies. Test replaces payload with a copy of the whole sample and metadata with the running member context. Other selected paths can resolve to wrong nonempty values. Equivalent live webhook delivery and renamed data/meta sample controls resolve correctly.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create a fresh workflow with a POST webhook trigger.
Set Expected Body to {"payload":{"id":"Sample title"},"metadata":{"label":"Sample body"},"plain":"Control"} and allow saving to finish.
Add Create Record for Notes. Use the variable picker to map Title to payload.id and Body to metadata.label; confirm that it previews Sample title and Sample body. Allow saving to finish.
Run Test Workflow and wait for completion. Inspect Create Record output and the created Note: Title is blank and Body lacks Sample body, despite the selected values being present in the saved sample.
Inspect trigger output to observe payload now contains the full sample object and metadata contains the running workspace member rather than the supplied metadata.label.
As a control, rename the sample parent keys to data and meta, select the corresponding fields again, save and Test; the Note receives both supplied values.

For the live-path comparison, activate an equivalent owned workflow with the original payload/metadata mappings and POST a body of the same field structure to its webhook URL. Verify the supplied values are preserved, then deactivate the demonstration workflow.

logicalBugs.explanation: Schedule intervals expressed as every N hours or days reset at calendar boundaries instead of preserving the requested elapsed interval. The retained interval and human-readable summary can disagree with upcoming trigger times.

rootCause.explanation: Schedule interval conversion encodes hours/days as cron */N fields. Cron restarts those fields each day/month instead of representing elapsed N-hour/N-day intervals, so advertised durations such as 25 hours or calendar-boundary days are not preserved.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Hours between triggers accepts and retains 25, but the generated cron schedule previews daily occurrences while the summary promises every 25 hours.

sourceBugs.name: A saved 25-hour workflow schedule is represented as daily cron occurrences

reproductionPaths.expected: An accepted Hours between triggers value should represent the stated interval, with its summary and upcoming execution times agreeing. Unsupported intervals should not be presented as a correctly configured every-N-hours schedule.
reproductionPaths.actual: The saved Hours value remains 25 and the summary says every 25 hours, but the next execution dates occur at the same time on consecutive days, only 24 hours apart. The contradiction persists after completed saves, reload and ordinary navigation. The backend generates the same hour-field cron pattern as the preview; actual scheduled executions were not observed.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create a fresh workflow with a scheduled trigger.
Choose Hours, enter 25 in Hours between triggers and set Trigger at minute (UTC) to 0. Move focus away and wait for the configuration to save.
Observe the every 25 hours summary alongside upcoming execution dates at midnight UTC on consecutive days. Those dates are 24 hours apart.
Reload and reopen the trigger, or navigate away and return. Confirm Hours remains 25 and the same summary/preview contradiction remains.
As controls, use 12 hours to obtain midnight/noon/midnight previews, or 24 hours to obtain daily previews that agree with the stated interval.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A saved three-day schedule preview crosses a month boundary with a one-day gap despite its every three days summary.

sourceBugs.name: Days schedule preview contradicts Days between triggers at calendar boundaries

reproductionPaths.expected: The ordinary Days between triggers form and its every N days summary should agree with successive preview intervals across calendar boundaries.
reproductionPaths.actual: A saved three-day schedule preview crosses a month boundary with a one-day gap despite its every three days summary. A saved 31-day variant previews 30-day and 31-day gaps.
reproSteps: Create a saved On a schedule workflow with Days interval and an ordinary positive integer Days between triggers value such as 3.
Use a late UTC time and inspect upcoming executions across a month boundary.
Observe a shorter boundary interval than the every N days form summary, then save/reload to confirm the retained configuration.
Control: Days 1 agrees with daily previews. A Days 31 setup provides another calendar-boundary mismatch when the visible dates expose it.

guidance.distinction: This entry covers the Days interval form at calendar boundaries; the existing entry covers Hours 25 conversion.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers the Days interval form at calendar boundaries; the existing entry covers Hours 25 conversion.

limitations: No missed or early actual scheduled execution was observed.
Not every current date necessarily exposes a mismatch within three preview rows.
Newer runtime was not tested.

logicalBugs.explanation: Duplicating a supported workflow without stored action positions, including seeded Quick Lead, gives copied action nodes the same canvas position so they obscure one another.

rootCause.explanation: Whole-workflow cloning copies per-step saved positions/default positions rather than reproducing the currently computed automatic layout, so duplicated actions stack when the source positions existed only in rendered layout.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Duplicating a supported workflow without stored action positions, including seeded Quick Lead, gives copied action nodes the same canvas position so they obscure one another.

sourceBugs.name: Duplicating an automatically laid-out workflow stacks copied action nodes

reproductionPaths.expected: Duplicating a workflow whose source graph is visibly separated should leave its copied actions separately visible and accessible, retaining or recomputing a usable layout for actions without saved coordinates.
reproductionPaths.actual: The source has separated nodes, but its duplicate stores copied action positions at the same point and displays overlapping cards, making covered actions appear missing. All actions, their data and linear connections remain present. The overlap persists on reload; Tidy up separates the nodes again.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and open the seeded Quick Lead workflow. Observe that its trigger and action nodes are visibly separated by the automatic layout.
Use Duplicate Workflow and open the newly created copy.
Observe that copied action nodes stack at one canvas position, with the top card obscuring other actions. Clicking the stack selects the top node rather than the covered nodes.
Reload or navigate away and return to confirm the overlapping layout persists.
Use Tidy up on an owned duplicate and allow the arranged node positions to save. Observe the separate nodes return with their configuration and connections intact.
As controls, duplicate that tidied copy or a fresh workflow drawn with saved canvas positions. Its copied nodes remain separated.

logicalBugs.explanation: At mobile and tablet widths, workflow Date and DateTime calendars can open beneath the fixed Form or Delay side panel, hiding the calendar and preventing day selection.

rootCause.explanation: The date/datetime floating picker portal does not establish a stacking level above the fixed mobile workflow/command panel. Its mounted calendar is painted beneath the panel despite being interactive in desktop context.

reproductionPaths.explanation: At viewport widths up to 768 pixels, a workflow Form Date calendar opens beneath the fixed form panel, preventing calendar day selection.

sourceBugs.name: Workflow Form date calendar is hidden behind the form on mobile and tablet

reproductionPaths.expected: Opening a Form Date picker on mobile or tablet should display the calendar above the form and allow a day to be selected.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390-pixel and 768-pixel widths, the calendar exists but is visually covered by the form panel. Ordinary clicks intended for calendar days hit the covering panel or dismiss the picker, leaving Date empty. At 769 pixels and desktop widths the calendar is visible and date selection works; a desktop control also submits the selected date successfully.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create an owned workflow with a Launch manually trigger and a Form action containing one Date field. Allow the configuration to save.
At a mobile viewport such as 390 by 844 CSS pixels, run Test and click the Date field to open its calendar.
Observe that the calendar is hidden behind the form panel. Attempt ordinary day selection and observe that the Date remains empty.
Repeat at a 768-pixel-wide viewport and observe the same covered calendar.
As controls, repeat at 769 pixels or a desktop width. The calendar appears above the form, a day can be selected, and Submit completes with the selected date.
The mobile failure can also be reproduced by activating the valid workflow and launching it directly through the Command Menu at 390 pixels, without resizing an already open desktop form.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The Delay date/time calendar opens beneath the mobile editor panel, preventing calendar selection while typed date entry still works.

sourceBugs.name: Delay date picker is hidden beneath the mobile workflow panel

reproductionPaths.expected: The Delay until date calendar opens visibly above the editor panel and accepts day selection on mobile and tablet.
reproductionPaths.actual: At tested 390px and 768px widths, focusing Delay until date mounts the calendar but its days are covered by the full-screen side panel. Clicking a covered day closes the picker without changing the date. Desktop selection and typed mobile date entry work.
reproSteps: Create a disposable manual workflow with a Delay action and select At a specific date or time.
At a 390px-wide viewport, open Delay until date and attempt to select a calendar day. Repeat with a fresh empty-date Delay and at tablet width.
Observe no visible calendar and no date change from the covered day click. Compare a wider desktop viewport and typing a date followed by reload.

guidance.distinction: Match the hidden date/time calendar in the mobile Delay action editor. Distinguish runtime Form Date calendars, keyboard clear/save behavior and calendars intentionally limited to navigation.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Match the hidden date/time calendar in the mobile Delay action editor. Distinguish runtime Form Date calendars, keyboard clear/save behavior and calendars intentionally limited to navigation.

limitations: Joint scope is the Delay editor’s At a specific date or time picker at tested mobile/tablet widths. Create Record, Calendar Event and other date-field callers are excluded.
The picker mounts but is covered; the absence is visual/pointer usability, not a failure to create day cells. Typed date entry works and persists.
The floating wrapper’s transform isolates the nested picker stacking from the fixed mobile side panel. Nested picker z-index values cannot be compared directly with the panel’s root z-index.

The related runtime Form Date entry uses a different component and entry point. It is dataset precedent, not an independently identified upstream maintainer acknowledgment of this exact editor defect.
Latest source also changes floating positioning strategy. Newer runtime and native touch were not tested; no targeted fix or linear ancestry claim is made.

logicalBugs.explanation: Changing an existing or placeholder workflow action to If/Else or Iterator saves companion nodes but omits them from the live diagram until reload. Adding routes or another node can then error or crash the editor.

rootCause.explanation: The action type-change service persists additionalCreatedSteps for complex If/Else and Iterator replacements but returns only updatedStep. useUpdateWorkflowVersionStep replaces that controller in client flow/cache without adding the saved companion nodes. The live diagram is therefore incomplete until reload; subsequent insertion traverses this incomplete graph. This is distinct from the persistent transient-ID Iterator return defect.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Changing an existing action to If/else saves its branch placeholders but omits them from the live canvas. Adding a route errors, and adding another node can crash the editor.

sourceBugs.name: Changing an action to If/else leaves missing branches and subsequent edits can crash the workflow editor

reproductionPaths.expected: The offered Change node type operation should produce a usable If/else graph with its branch placeholders, as direct creation does. Subsequent route and node additions should work without crashing.
reproductionPaths.actual: After converting a Delay to If/else, the canvas shows only the trigger and converted action, with no branch placeholders. Add route displays Invalid Configuration. On a fresh converted workflow, Add a Node > If/else produces the full-page Sorry, something went wrong error screen. The server has saved the branches correctly; reloading restores them and recovers editing.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create an owned workflow with a Launch manually trigger and a Delay action. Allow saves to complete.
Use the Delay action menu to choose Change node type, then select If/else. Wait for the successful save.
Observe that the converted If/else node has no branch action placeholders on the canvas. In its settings, click Add route and observe Invalid Configuration.
On a second fresh workflow, repeat the saved Delay-to-If/else conversion without clicking Add route. Use the top Add a Node command and choose If/else.
Observe the editor is replaced by Sorry, something went wrong and asks for a page refresh.

Reload the workflow and observe the saved branch placeholders return and editing recovers. As a control, add If/else directly to a fresh workflow: its initial branches, Add route, and subsequent node creation work.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After converting an existing Else or Iterator-child placeholder to Iterator, subsequent Filter or Create Record insertion can replace the workflow editor with a recoverable page error.

sourceBugs.name: Adding an action after converting an existing placeholder to Iterator crashes the workflow editor

reproductionPaths.expected: Adding an offered action after placeholder-to-Iterator conversion should keep the editor usable.
reproductionPaths.actual: After replacing an existing If/Else Else placeholder with Iterator, adding a disconnected Filter through header Add a Node replaces the workflow editor with Sorry, something went wrong / Please refresh the page. Two fresh workflows reproduce; reload retains the saved Filter and restores editable configuration. Connected Filter insertion through the converted Iterator loop connector also crashes before reload. Converting an outer Iterator child placeholder to a nested Iterator and choosing Create Record from its loop handle produces the same editor crash on two fresh workflows; reload recovers.
reproSteps: Create an owned manual workflow containing Code and If/Else.
Replace the existing Else branch placeholder with Iterator, preserving the live diagram without reload.
Use the header Add a Node action to add a disconnected Filter. Observe the main editor crash while the navigation sidebar remains.
Reload to recover and configure the saved Filter; compare connected branch Filter insertion and header insertion after reload.

Additional verified variation: After converting an Else placeholder to Iterator, insert Filter from the loop connector instead of the header. Create a manual workflow with an If/Else action. Configure a condition and change its Else placeholder action to Iterator. Set Iterator items to Alpha and Beta and leave the editor to save. Without reloading the workflow, drag the Iterator loop connector onto blank canvas and choose Filter. Observe the page-content error instead of Filter Conditions. Reload; the saved Filter can then be opened and edited. Compare a fresh Iterator created directly from Add Node: dragging its loop connector and choosing Filter opens Conditions successfully, including with saved Alpha and Beta items.

Additional verified variation: Convert an outer Iterator child placeholder into a nested Iterator, then insert Create Record from its loop handle. Create a manual workflow with an outer Iterator and two literal items. Select its existing Add an Action child placeholder and change its action type to Iterator. Drag from the inner Iterator’s loop handle to open Select Action, then choose Create Record. Observe the full-page error. Reload to recover. Compare a fresh nested Iterator created through the outer loop edge’s plus insertion control; adding its Create Record action keeps the editor usable.

guidance.distinction: One reference covers editor crashes after converting an existing Else or Iterator-child placeholder to Iterator, then adding a Filter through the header or loop connector, or Create Record through the nested loop handle. These are compatible insertion variations, not separate discovery targets. Do not require every route. Ordinary If/Else conversion remains N45 coverage; missing loop returns and execution after one item remain N51 coverage. No shared exact crash mechanism across all routes is established.

matchingGuidance.distinction: One reference covers editor crashes after converting an existing Else or Iterator-child placeholder to Iterator, then adding a Filter through the header or loop connector, or Create Record through the nested loop handle. These are compatible insertion variations, not separate discovery targets. Do not require every route. Ordinary If/Else conversion remains N45 coverage; missing loop returns and execution after one item remain N51 coverage. No shared exact crash mechanism across all routes is established.

limitations: Iterator conversion is the new related trigger; ordinary If/Else conversion crashes remain existing N45 coverage and add no separate yield.
Two fresh workflows share one fixture. No execution failure, lost mappings or direct sparse-memory observation is claimed.
Codex-only approval; no independent Claude agreement is represented. Latest runtime was not tested.

logicalBugs.explanation: Delay inspectors in completed runs and archived workflow versions expose Delete and Duplicate despite being read-only. These actions create or change the current workflow draft instead of editing the displayed historical graph.

rootCause.explanation: WorkflowEditActionDelay disables its inputs for readonly views but always renders WorkflowStepFooter without a readonly guard. Delete/Duplicate therefore obtain an updatable current draft even when invoked from a historical/active inspector.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Delay inspectors in completed runs and archived workflow versions expose Delete and Duplicate despite being read-only. These actions create or change the current workflow draft instead of editing the displayed historical graph.

sourceBugs.name: Historical Delay Delete and Duplicate controls modify the current workflow draft

reproductionPaths.expected: Read-only run and historical-version inspectors should not expose step mutation controls. Editing from a historical version should require an explicit Use as draft transition and target the version the user chose to edit.
reproductionPaths.actual: A completed run shows disabled Delay fields but enabled Delete and Options controls. Deleting the historical Delay creates or updates the current draft with that step removed, while the run graph remains unchanged. Archived-version Delete and Duplicate likewise target current configuration; a duplicate can use the current Delay value rather than the historical value displayed. Changes persist after successful mutation responses, navigation, and reload. The published active version and historical records remain unchanged.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace administrator and create an owned workflow with a Launch manually trigger and a short Delay. Allow saving to complete, activate the workflow, and complete a run.
Open the completed run, select its Delay node, and open the Node tab. Observe disabled settings alongside enabled Delete and Options controls.
Click Delete in that historical Delay inspector. The historical run graph still contains its Delay.
Use See Workflow to open current configuration. Observe a new draft, or a change to an existing draft, with the Delay removed. Reload and confirm the draft change persists.

logicalBugs.explanation: Choosing Iterator in an If/else branch placeholder or changing an existing action to Iterator generates a loop child whose return references a nonexistent step. The saved workflow fails after processing its first item.

rootCause.explanation: Type replacement creates an Iterator with a fresh transient ID and constructs its loop return referencing that ID, then overrides only the controller ID with the existing placeholder ID. Loop references still point at the absent transient controller, breaking iteration or skipped-path continuation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Choosing Iterator in an If/else branch placeholder or changing an existing action to Iterator generates a loop child whose return references a nonexistent step. The saved workflow fails after processing its first item.

reproductionPaths.actual: After choosing Iterator in an If/else branch, its generated loop controls are initially missing from the canvas. Refresh reveals the saved child, but the loop return still targets a transient ID that does not belong to any saved step. A Test with two successfully saved items processes the first item, then fails on the missing destination. The empty loop body itself succeeds and is supported; a directly added top-level Iterator with the same two items completes both. Changing a top-level Delay to Iterator reproduces the malformed return too. Replacing the revealed loop child with a one-second Delay does not repair the saved return: the Delay succeeds for item one, then the run fails before item two. A directly added Iterator with the same Delay completes both items.

Set the IF condition to Metadata > Workspace Member ID > Is not empty so the branch is taken.
Click that branch Add an Action placeholder and choose Iterator. Enter and commit two literal items, 1 and 2, then allow saving to complete before leaving its settings.
Observe the loop action placeholder is initially absent. Reload or navigate away and back to reveal the saved loop child. Leave that loop body empty for this reproduction.

Run Test after the items and graph have saved. Observe the first item is reached, the empty body succeeds, and the run fails before the second item because the saved loop return references a nonexistent step. Reopening does not repair this saved connection.

An alternate entry point is to add a top-level Delay and use Change node type > Iterator. Configure and save the same two items; its generated loop return also references a missing step.

A directly added top-level Iterator with the same two items and one-second Delay executes the Delay twice and completes.

A completed response updates the flow using its captured submitted trigger, and the controlled input synchronizes to that echoed value. An older response can restore a stale prefix; the minute handler copies that stale hour into its next save. Exact server commit ordering is not independently traced.

reproductionPaths.actual: Fast entry of 23 can leave the hour field and preview at 2/02:00 even while a saved readback still holds 23. Changing only Minutes then saves hour 2 with the new minute. Reloading and reopening retains the wrong hour and preview.

Replace the hour with 23 using fast ordinary typing; wait for saves. Repeat if needed until the field and preview show 2/02:00.

Compare normal-speed entry, a one-digit hour edit, and retyping the intended hour; these controls preserve the intended setting.

logicalBugs.explanation: Typing a Delay duration and pressing Tab leaves focus in the same input, so its blur-based save never runs and reload restores the old duration.

rootCause.explanation: Delay stores duration edits locally and calls its action update only on blur. The number input uses TextInput hotkeys with no Tab callback. The default handler prevents the native Tab action, so focus stays in the input, blur never occurs and no duration update is submitted.

logicalBugs.explanation: Rapidly updating two numeric duration fields in a Delay action causes the second input to revert to its previously saved value. Waiting between edits allows each value to save.

rootCause.explanation: Each Delay duration blur submits a full duration object captured from local state. An earlier update response synchronizes action/localDuration while a second field edit is pending, so the later commit can spread an older sibling value over the newer edit.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Rapidly updating two numeric duration fields in a Delay action causes the second input to revert to its previously saved value. Waiting between edits allows each value to save.

reproductionPaths.actual: Second field edits are overwritten by an earlier field's save/re-render. Reproduced twice with different values, confirmed in saved run input and after reopening the action. Editing the second field alone and waiting saves it correctly.
reproSteps: Create a disposable saved workflow with a Delay set to Minutes 0 and Seconds 3.

rootCause.explanation: Parent restoration undeletes automated trigger records as well as versions. logicalBugs.explanation: Deleting a workflow during a pending Delay and restoring it after the deadline can strand the original run at Running/Pending with downstream actions unstarted. A new run of the restored same-version workflow completes normally.

rootCause.explanation: Workflow restore undeletes run/version records but does not recreate the expired/consumed delayed resume job. resume-delayed-workflow can ignore or terminate work while its run is deleted, leaving the later restored run RUNNING/PENDING after the scheduled resume time.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After deletion during a pending Delay and restoration beyond its deadline, bounded observations show the original run still Running/Pending with its downstream action unstarted. A new run of the restored same-version configuration completes normally.

sourceBugs.name: Restored workflow run remains pending beyond Delay while healthy control completes

reproductionPaths.expected: Deletion/restoration should leave a run in a coherent waiting or terminal state rather than a pending state whose expired Delay no longer advances. This entry does not require automatic resumption as the only acceptable lifecycle policy.
reproductionPaths.actual: After deletion during a pending Delay and restoration beyond its deadline, bounded observations show the original run still Running/Pending with its downstream action unstarted. A new run of the restored same-version configuration completes normally.
reproSteps: Create a disposable manual workflow with Delay 15 seconds followed by a harmless Create Note action.
Test and delete the workflow while its Delay is pending. Leave it deleted beyond the configured deadline.
Restore the workflow, reopen the same run and reload. At bounded follow-up checks, observe Running/Pending with the downstream action unstarted.
Test the restored workflow without deleting it as a control and confirm the same Delay duration completes normally.
